gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the BLUETTI Apex 300's own solar inputs accept only 12–60 V, so each input takes one 46.5 V Voc 350 W panel (or several in parallel) and can't take panels in series. To get past that you need BLUETTI's $699 SolarX 4K controller, which won't start below a 150 V string, meaning at least 4 of those panels in series, carries at most 13 A (one string of those panels), and also needs a 600 V/20 A PV disconnect and a ground cable that aren't in the box.
standout_why: Compared against the three cited pages. EnergySage lists the Apex 300 with two 200 W panels at $2,099 and only says to stay 'within the unit's voltage and wattage limits', with no voltage numbers and no mention of SolarX. Solar Waypoint (F3800 Plus vs DELTA Pro Ultra) gives input voltage windows for those two units only and says nothing on wiring, the Apex 300 or SolarX. thisWATT would not load (SSL certificate error), so I couldn't compare against it. None of these pages says how many panels to put in series, the 150 V start-up minimum, the 13 A single-string limit, or the missing disconnect and ground. Those facts decide which BLUETTI bundle and how many panels work.
kit_items: Power station: BLUETTI Apex 300 (2,764.8 Wh LFP, 3,840 W, 120/240 V from one unit through a NEMA 14-50R per StorageReview). ChatGPT showed it as a catalog card, it is on an approved program (awin:bluetti_us) and it is already listed on Dealectric.
Expansion battery: BLUETTI B300K, bundled to reach 5,529.6 Wh. That is a small-cabin size by ChatGPT's own sizing table.
High-voltage solar controller: BLUETTI SolarX 4K (150–500 V in, up to 4,000 W). Without it the Apex 300 is limited to its 12–60 V inputs, so panels can't go in series.

Panels: at least 4 BLUETTI 350 W panels in series (4 × 46.5 V = 186 V Voc, 4 × 37.5 V = 150 V Vmp, inside SolarX's 120–450 V MPPT range). Only one string, because two strings would draw 18.4 A against the 13 A limit.
Not in any bundle, buy separately: a 600 V/20 A PV disconnect, a grounding cable, and a covered wall to mount SolarX vertically, because it isn't weatherproof (Notebookcheck).
Optional: BLUETTI Hub D1, because the Apex 300 has no USB or 12 V ports on its own (StorageReview: $299).

findings.label: Panel electricals
findings.value: Voc 46.5 V, Vmp 37.5 V, Isc 10.8 A, Imp 9.2 A, MC4
findings.source_title: StorageReview, BLUETTI PV350 solar panel review (Kevin OBrien, 2023-09-22)
findings.note: Arithmetic: 1 panel is 46.5 V, under the Apex's 60 V limit, but 2 in series is 93 V, over it, so on the built-in inputs panels can only be paralleled. Into SolarX, 4 in series gives 186 V Voc and 150 V Vmp, which is the minimum. Two parallel strings give Imp 18.4 A, over the 13 A limit, so only one string. 10 in series is 465 V Voc at standard test conditions, close to the 500 V limit before any cold-weather rise.
